name: From Apes to Humans
description: Seven million years of bones, footprints and stone tools, from the first upright walkers to the many kinds of human that came before us.

checkpoints.name: First steps
checkpoints.note: The oldest ancestors, such as Sahelanthropus and Ardipithecus, begin to walk upright while still climbing in trees.

checkpoints.name: Walkers and toolmakers
checkpoints.note: Australopithecines such as Lucy walk the African savanna, leaving footprints at Laetoli, and the first stone tools appear.

checkpoints.name: The genus Homo
checkpoints.note: Homo habilis and Homo erectus make better tools, tame fire and spread out of Africa across Asia and Europe.

checkpoints.name: Many kinds of human
checkpoints.note: Homo sapiens, Neanderthals, Homo naledi and the hobbit of Flores share the world, and only our species survives.

checkpoints.name: Darwin's idea
checkpoints.note: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species and starts the science of human evolution.
